newsitem.title: CHINA: Handover parties take toll on HK flag creator.
newsitem.headline: Handover parties take toll on HK flag creator.

text.p: The Chinese professor who designed Hong Kong's post-colonial flag had to be treated in hospital for fatigue after too many handover parties, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.

Xiao Hong, a professor in Zhengzhou city in central China's Henan province, won a national competition to design a Hong Kong flag with his crimson banner sporting a white bauhinia blossom, Xinhua said.
Hong Kong's British-designed flag will be lowered when the colony returns to Beijing rule at midnight on June 30.
The glory of designing the new Hong Kong flag had taken its toll on Xiao, the agency said.

"Almost every local meeting connected to Hong Kong's return in Zhengzhou city... had asked him to be present until recently, when the poor man fell ill and was hospitalised for nine days because of fatigue," it said.
Xiao's creation can be seen almost everywhere in China as government offices, companies and local residents are swept up in a state-sponsored patriotic frenzy surrounding the handover.
